svg.title: What choudoufu keeps, and where
svg.desc: choudoufu keeps two things. A marker on every resource says which estate owns it and which configuration block it belongs to; the apply writes it on the create call, and it is the only thing that says what you own. A record per resource holds what cannot be read back from the live object; choudoufu writes it to the record store, which is a local directory, an S3 bucket or Secrets in a cluster. A state file is still written on the machine that ran, as a cache that may be deleted.
svg.text: written on the create call. Any cloud tool
can read it, and your IAM can condition on it
holds what cannot be read back
one per resource: a password the API never
returns, a random name, a script that ran
a local directory, an S3 bucket,
And a state file, as a cache
on the machine that ran. Never asked who owns what. Delete it and the next plan gives the same answer
